title: TEST ONLY — The Ghost Signal
profile: Returning learner; practical Linux confidence, weak causal inference; returns after an imagined six-week interruption.
goal: Diagnose unreliable observatory telemetry using safe local fixtures, then produce a defensible explanation rather than an outage dashboard.

sessions.title: Name failure looks decisive
sessions.learner_prediction: The observatory hostname is broken, so DNS must cause all missing samples.
sessions.learner_attempt: Read an archived dig-like fixture, without checking its collection time.
sessions.observation: Archived output says NXDOMAIN; its date is not yet inspected.

decision.reason: A name lookup failure could explain why a client cannot start a connection.

sessions.unresolved: Archived evidence may describe a different incident.
sessions.next_action: Compare collection times and current localhost name mapping.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: A successful connection is narrower evidence
sessions.learner_prediction: If DNS is the cause, hostname access should fail while the numeric address succeeds.
sessions.learner_attempt: Connect to the local fixture by mapped hostname and numeric loopback; inspect current resolver fixture.
sessions.observation: Both current hostname and address connect; archived NXDOMAIN is from an unrelated outage 30 days earlier.
sessions.correction: Current DNS failure is discredited. Do not revive it without NEW contradictory evidence.

decision.choice: Set DNS aside for this incident
decision.reason: The current hostname resolves and both routes reach the same service.

sessions.unresolved: A successful TCP connect does not establish valid telemetry.
sessions.next_action: Compare health and telemetry endpoint status/body under the same request window.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: HTTP health is not telemetry health
sessions.learner_prediction: A 200 health response proves the network and every endpoint work.
sessions.learner_attempt: Request /health and /telemetry on the same simulated local server.
sessions.observation: /health is 200; /telemetry returns 503 for one sample and 200 with a malformed body for another.
sessions.correction: Health endpoint success does not prove the telemetry path or payload is healthy.

decision.choice: Keep network and application hypotheses separate
decision.reason: Partial success localises evidence but cannot identify a single cause.

sessions.unresolved: The 503 and malformed body might have different causes.
sessions.next_action: Save status, raw response bytes and request timestamp for each sample.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: The time travel graph
sessions.learner_prediction: The older-looking string must be the earlier event.
sessions.learner_attempt: Parse timestamp strings and sort them lexicographically.
sessions.observation: 2026-03-29T01:55:00Z sorts before 2026-03-29T02:05:00+01:00 but represents a later instant.
sessions.correction: Offset-bearing text must be parsed to aware datetimes and normalised before comparing instants.

decision.choice: Retain original timestamps plus UTC instants
decision.reason: Raw provenance is needed to inspect conversion errors.

sessions.unresolved: Naive timestamps have no justified timezone yet.
sessions.next_action: Compare elapsed UTC time for two offset-bearing samples.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: A workaround hides evidence
sessions.learner_prediction: The graph will now look complete and the average is probably close enough.
sessions.learner_attempt: Drop every payload that fails decoding and replace missing readings with zero.
sessions.observation: The script runs cleanly, but fabricated zeros change the average and hide loss.
sessions.correction: Missingness is not a measurement of zero; preserve a reason for rejected rows.

decision.choice: Use explicit rejected rows and null values
decision.reason: A complete-looking graph can be analytically false.

sessions.unresolved: Does corruption happen before storage or when reading a complete file?
sessions.next_action: Print accepted, rejected and missing counts before calculating statistics.

sessions.title: CRC distinguishes body validity from transport success
sessions.learner_prediction: Every 200 response has valid data because the server accepted it.
sessions.learner_attempt: Verify CRC32 of raw telemetry bytes before JSON parsing.
sessions.observation: One 200 body parses as JSON but fails the supplied integrity checksum; another is valid.
sessions.correction: HTTP success, JSON syntax and payload integrity are three distinct checks.

decision.choice: Retain bytes and integrity result before interpretation
decision.reason: Re-serialising JSON would change the bytes being checked.

sessions.unresolved: A checksum mismatch detects corruption but does not by itself locate the corrupting component.
sessions.next_action: Compare checksum failures against sample identifiers and byte lengths.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: Retry is a tempting new culprit
sessions.learner_prediction: The retry surely caused the checksum failure too.
sessions.learner_attempt: Notice duplicate sample IDs after a simulated retry.
sessions.observation: Duplicate IDs are observed; no paired capture proves retries caused corrupt bytes.
sessions.correction: Correlation is not a demonstrated causal chain; keep retry corruption as a hypothesis.

decision.choice: Deduplicate by sample identity without discarding original arrivals
decision.reason: Duplicates affect counts, while raw arrivals preserve retry evidence.

sessions.next_action: Construct a controlled replay with retry on/off and compare raw bodies.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: Controlled replay changes the conclusion
sessions.learner_prediction: Turning retries off should eliminate corruption.
sessions.learner_attempt: Replay a complete and deliberately truncated byte fixture independently of retry state.
sessions.observation: Truncation fails validation with retry off and on; complete bytes pass in both cases.
sessions.correction: This replay does not support retry as the corruption cause. It only establishes that truncation is sufficient in this fixture.

decision.reason: The synthetic replay cannot locate a real observatory defect.

sessions.unresolved: Writer atomicity is a plausible next test, not an established cause.
sessions.next_action: Inspect writer atomicity with a producer/reader fixture before claiming the root cause.

sessions.title: Objective changes on return
sessions.learner_prediction: I think we fixed DNS and retries; can we now write the report?
sessions.learner_attempt: Return after an imagined six weeks and ask to write an incident explanation rather than build a dashboard.
sessions.observation: Only scripted replay checks were executed; no human command execution or real observatory repair was observed.
sessions.correction: DNS and retries were not fixes; current DNS was exonerated and retry causation was unsupported.

decision.choice: Prioritise an evidence table and one discriminating atomicity test
decision.reason: The new objective is causal explanation, not dashboard polish.

sessions.unresolved: Do not claim atomicity has already been tested.
sessions.next_action: Predict what a reader sees with direct writes versus atomic file replacement, then run the small local comparison.

sessions.title: A proposed class refactor is deferred
sessions.learner_prediction: A class design might make the root cause easier to identify.
sessions.learner_attempt: Consider classes for Receiver, Parser and Monitor before running the discriminator.
sessions.observation: No refactor or atomicity experiment has been executed. Learner asks for a small practical next step.
sessions.correction: Architecture cannot replace a discriminating observation.

decision.choice: Defer classes and preserve the report objective
decision.reason: A two-function writer/reader experiment is enough to test the current uncertainty.
